The mark is derived from the log and never written. A card is stale when a card it depends on, or its parent, changed after the link existed, and the card has no review since. A link made after the change carries no mark (#vi-prop-bornstale). A review ends in a confirm or an amend (#rederive-reason). A card whose basis is stale waits. It is not stale (#map-wait).

A reopen with reason postponed marks cards paused, not stale. The paused mark reaches every card downstream, at any distance (#pr-wf-paused). A paused card is never reviewed, so a pause that moved one hop would stop at the first card.

Staleness spreads one hop on purpose. The rule is on #vi-prop.

**Why children go stale.** A child card is part of its parent. If the parent changes, the child may no longer be true. So an amend or reopen of a card marks:

1. Every card that has a `depends_on` link to it.
2. Every direct child (`refines`) of it.

**Why a parent sometimes goes stale.** Staleness travels along `depends_on` and parent-to-child links. A parent turns stale when it has a `depends_on` link to the changed card. It also turns stale when its own parent changed. It does not turn stale just because a child changed. Check the trace on the marked card. It shows the changed card and the link.

**Why only one hop.** A review that leaves a card unchanged stops the mark there. A review that changes the card is a change too, so the mark moves one more hop. Marking every dependent at any distance would mark dozens of cards for a one-word edit (rejected as #vi-prop:opt-anydistance).

Two exceptions:

- A link made after the change carries no mark (#vi-prop-bornstale).
- A card on a stale basis waits. It does not show as stale (#map-wait).

The design does include that step. It is the review in #rederive-reason. An agent reads each stale card and its link reasons. It then confirms the card, or it amends the card. A confirm stops the spread at that card. Only an amend moves the mark one more hop.

I found no card that starts this review by itself. When a change marks cards, the marks stay until someone runs the review. The agent may confirm any card. Nothing makes it do so after each change. I searched the map for stale and review cards only, so a card under another name could exist.

So the spread is controlled in one way. The mark goes one hop, and a confirm ends it. The check that the cards still hold is not automatic yet.

Two ways to close the gap:

1. **Review after each change (recommended).** When a reopen or an amend marks cards, the agent reviews every marked card in the same turn. It confirms the ones that hold. It proposes an amend for the others. A confirm already needs each link reason read (#vi-prop-confirm-names), so a blind confirm is refused.
2. **Review on request.** Marks stay until you ask. This is the behaviour now.

A confirm names each depends_on target whose link reason the reviewer read

To keep a confirm from clearing a mark unread, the confirm carries the list of depends_on targets whose reasons the reviewer read. The list must hold every target whose link was made before the newest stale mark on the card. A link made after that change needs no entry. A target with no depends_on link from the card is refused. A refusal names each unread link with its reason, and gives the confirm again with the full list.

Example. Four cards:
- A is "We charge per seat".
- B is "The invoice shows the seat count". It depends on A.
- D is "Invoices are in EUR".
- C is "The invoice PDF has a seat column". It depends on B and on D.

A change marks the next hop (#vi-prop). Left alone, the marks stay until someone reviews them, and a map with many marks stops being read. To avoid this, the agent that made the change reviews every card the change marked, before the turn ends.

For each marked card the agent reads the card, the changed card, and the reason on each link between them. Then it ends the review in one of the two ways that #rederive-reason defines. A card that still holds gets a confirm, which clears the mark and stops the spread there. A card that no longer holds gets a proposal to amend it. The person accepts or discards the proposal. An amend of a card that the person decides (who: you) is never applied by the agent alone.

I proposed #vi-prop-auto-review under #vi-prop. It is not in the map until you accept it.

- **Rule:** after a change, the agent reads each marked card and its link reasons in the same turn. It confirms the cards that hold and proposes an amend for the rest. It skips a card that waits on a stale basis.
- **Links:** the card depends on #rederive-reason, #vi-prop-confirm-names and #map-wait. Those links are held until you accept it.
- **Rejected option:** "marks stay until a person asks" is recorded as an alternative.
- **Kill criterion:** a manual check. If a card the agent confirmed turns out wrong later, the review is too loose.
- **Ticket watch:** every command printed "the ticket watch failed: no free ticket number from 01 to 99 in werk". The card was added anyway. The ticket numbers are used up and need a fix.

## Say so when a card you just made comes out stale

A change marks the next hop only: its direct dependents and its direct children. A link made
after the change carries no mark from it. So a new card is not marked stale by a reopen that came
before its links. If the server marks it anyway, the server runs old code: restart
`werk serve`.

A new card can still depend on a target that is stale now. Then the card waits. It is not
stale. Say it in the same turn: name the stale target, and say the card was
written with that correction already in hand.

Run `werk show <id>` after you create a card. It prints the whole trace — origin,
reason, date, the hops. If a mark remains, either clear it,

```bash
werk rederive <id> --status decided
```

or leave it and say why not. Do not leave a red mark unexplained.

card vi-prop-confirm-names  [open]
A confirm names each depends_on target whose link reason the reviewer read
why: A confirm must show that each outgoing link reason was checked, and the program cannot see a reading. So the confirm lists the targets of the links it read, and the program compares that list with the links that were there before the change.
subtree: 1 card, 1 open

To keep a confirm from clearing a mark unread, the confirm carries the list of depends_on targets whose reasons the reviewer read. The list must hold every target whose link was made before the newest stale mark on the card. A link made after that change needs no entry. A target with no depends_on link from the card is refused. A refusal names each unread link with its reason, and gives the confirm again with the full list.

Example. Four cards:
- A is "We charge per seat".
- B is "The invoice shows the seat count". It depends on A.
- D is "Invoices are in EUR".
- C is "The invoice PDF has a seat column". It depends on B and on D.

What happens:
1. B is reopened and decided again. C goes stale.
2. A confirm of C that lists B only is refused. The refusal names the link C to D and its reason.
3. A confirm of C that lists B and D passes. C clears.
4. A link from C made after step 1 would not need to be listed.

```
 C --depends_on--> B --depends_on--> A
 C --depends_on--> D

 confirm C [B]      refused: the reason of C -> D is not confirmed
 confirm C [B, D]   C clears
```

**`--amend`**

- An amend is the second way to end a review (#rederive-reason). The card does not hold, so the reviewer changes it.
- The sentence says what changed, for example "seat count is now a user count".

- `--confirm all` means "I read every outgoing link". It saves typing the full list.

A decided card is frozen (#map-frozen), so `rederive` was never the way to change its content. The change goes through a proposal:

1. The agent runs `werk propose <id>` with the new title, why or body.
2. Accepting the proposal is the amend. It reopens and decides the card in one step.
3. The amend clears the card's own stale mark, because it is the review of that card.
4. It marks the next hop, so the dependents of the card go stale and get their own review.

This is the path I built. So `rederive` only confirms. It has no amend ending.

`--amend "<what changed>"` on `rederive` would add a second way to the same result. It would also need the new text, and `rederive` has no place for it. The only thing it adds is a sentence in the trace of the marked cards. #werk-cli-reopen-flags gets that sentence with `werk propose --review "..."` on the same proposal.
